transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Mark Chen (CTO, Ursa), Elena Ruiz (Head of ML), Omar Al-Khalil (Infra), Sofia Park (PM)

Summary: quick intake to understand cost targets, hosting constraints (VPC/on-prem), and pilot scope. Customer is evaluating hosted vs. dedicated vs. private for both chat generation and embedding pipelines. Primary concerns: per-token unit cost at scale, latency SLOs during market hours, caching effectiveness on templated prompts, and compliance/KMS.

Topics: per-token pricing, batching and prefix/KV caching, reserved capacity economics, fallback strategies, SOC2+KMS, pilot metrics and timeline

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, excited to talk through the economics side and hosting options. Quick go-round on roles?
[00:07] Mark Chen: Mark here, CTO. We're trying to figure out if Redwood Hosted is cost-effective for our market data chat assistant, or if we should push for Dedicated or Private.
[00:14] Elena Ruiz: Hi, Elena. Looking at embeddings at scale too — nightly indexing and realtime similarity for search.
[00:19] Omar Al-Khalil: Omar, infra. Main ask: we need VPC controls and ability to bring our own KMS.
[00:25] Alex Morgan: Great. Priya and Lena from our side — Priya is going to cover perf/batching stuff.
[00:30] Priya Desai: Hey all. I'll jump in on batching, caching, and latency tradeoffs.
[00:35] Sofia Park: Sofia, PM, focused on budget and timeline.

[00:45] Priya Desai: Can you give us high-level traffic profile? qps, prompt lengths, percent of templated prompts?
[00:50] Mark Chen: Sure — baseline is 25 qps outside market hours, spikes to ~320 qps for 10-15 minutes at market open/close. Typical prompt length 120-180 tokens for chat. Embeddings job: nightly bulk of about 6 million texts, avg text length ~350 tokens.
[01:10] Alex Morgan: Good detail. On hosted per-token pricing, we showed list pricing in the deck; for heavy bursty load and embedding batches there's two levers — batching and prefix caching. If you have templated prompts we can get high cache hit rates which reduces tokens billed.
[01:28] Elena Ruiz: How does that look numerically? If we have, say, 40% cache hits on chat what does per-interaction cost become?
[01:35] Priya Desai: Roughly — assuming a model at our mid-tier, with per-input and per-output token rates, a 40% prefix hit can drop billed tokens by 30-45% depending on output length. For embeddings, if you batch 1k sequences per GPU and use parallel cross-batch packing, unit costs can fall by 3x vs naive single-request runs.
[01:58] Mark Chen: When you say "mid-tier" model, can you name an example?
[02:03] Priya Desai: Example model families we typically recommend for that latency/cost balance are open-vic or redwood-compat mid-range variants — we call them out in the catalog with perf profiles. (background noise) 
[02:15] Mark Chen: Ok. About dedicated — if we reserve capacity, what's the commit vs burst math?
[02:22] Alex Morgan: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools; you commit to a baseline throughput and get lower effective per-token cost because GPU time is unit-priced differently. You still pay for reserved capacity month-to-month, but burst options can be configured. Typically customers with predictable daytime spikes buy a dedicated baseline sized for the 95th percentile and use burst for the top 5-10% peaks.
[02:48] Omar Al-Khalil: We are regulated — KMS and audit logs are hard requirements. Hosted sometimes triggers red flags with our security team. Can Redwood Hosted do customer-managed KMS?
[02:57] Alex Morgan: On Hosted we offer envelope encryption and an option for customer-supplied keys in some regions, but for strict control we recommend Dedicated with private control plane or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). We'll share the SOC2 and KMS docs.
[03:12] Sofia Park: Budget — we have an internal target of $X per 1k chats during peak. I don't want to say the exact number on this call, but it's tight. How do we model per-1k costs across Hosted vs Dedicated?
[03:24] Priya Desai: You model by taking average tokens per request * token price and then apply effective reductions from caching and batching. For Dedicated, you amortize reserved compute cost across tokens produced. We can run a spreadsheet with your qps/tokens profile to show the crossover point.
[03:40] Mark Chen: Can you run a sensitivity on cache hit rate from 0% to 60%? We use lots of templated prompts for the chat assistant and expect high repeat prefixes.
[03:48] Priya Desai: Absolutely, for templated prompts the marginal benefit is big. We'll include three cache scenarios in the pricing sheet (low/med/high).

[04:05] Elena Ruiz: For embeddings: our nightly job — we care mostly about throughput and total cost, latency is not as critical. Any tips?
[04:12] Priya Desai: For bulk embed, use dedicated batching, pack sequences, and set quantized models where acceptable. Also, sharding across multiple GPUs and using our optimized kernels keeps throughput up while lowering cost. If you can accept 8-bit quant models there is a significant price drop. We'll show quantization recommendations per workload.
[04:33] Mark Chen: Is there any accuracy impact with 8-bit quant? Elena?
[04:37] Elena Ruiz: Slightly, but for semantic search it may be fine; we'll want to run evals.

[04:50] Omar Al-Khalil: From infra side, how isolated is Dedicated? Network wise. Can we get VPC peering and private endpoints?
[04:58] Alex Morgan: Dedicated has VPC options and private endpoints; Redwood Private gives you the full private control plane. We'll share the deployment checklist.

[05:12] Priya Desai: One other lever — request routing. You can route low-latency interactive requests to a smaller model hosted in region and fall back to a higher-quality model in Dedicated during off hours or non-critical queries to control cost. That's a common hybrid pattern.
[05:30] Mark Chen: That sounds interesting. Can you do automatic fallback if Dedicated is at capacity?
[05:35] Alex Morgan: Yes, smart routing and fallback policies are supported — we can configure cost-based routing, latency-first routing, or tier-based fallbacks. We'll include routing options in the playbook.

[05:50] Sofia Park: Pilot timeline — we want a quick proof: 2 weeks to validate latency at 95/99 and cost per 1k chats. Is that realistic?
[05:58] Priya Desai: Yes — typical POC is 2-3 weeks: day 0-3 provisioning and instrumenting, day 4-10 perf runs including market open/close windows, day 11-14 report and recommendations. We'll need your sample prompts and traffic replay or synthetic driver.
[06:16] Mark Chen: We can provide anonymized prompt sets and traffic logs.
[06:20] Alex Morgan: Perfect. We'll also run a benchmark simulating the market open spike to hit your peak qps so caching behaviors are visible.

[06:30] Elena Ruiz: One more question — how do you bill for cache hits? I want to be sure we're not double charged.
[06:36] Priya Desai: You only pay for the tokens we actually fetch/compute. If prefix is served from cache the input tokens that are repeated won't be billed; billing reflects tokens executed. There are implementation caveats but we'll document exact billing semantics.
[06:52] Mark Chen: What about embedding costs for 6M nightly — do you offer a bulk discount or reserved batch windows?
[06:58] Alex Morgan: For large periodic workloads we can recommend reserved batch slots, which are cheaper. Also, if you commit to monthly volume (Dedicated reserved capacity), we can give a tiered discount. We'll show an amortized per-embedding cost in the spreadsheet.

[07:15] Sofia Park: Regarding compliance, we need retention controls. Can logs/audit be turned off or restricted per team?
[07:22] Alex Morgan: Yes, per-role RBAC and audit log retention is configurable, and Private deployments give you the most control. We'll include retention settings and the default hosted retention policy.

[07:36] Omar Al-Khalil: Are there SLA differences between Hosted and Dedicated?
[07:40] Alex Morgan: Hosted has standard availability metrics; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency commitments in enterprise plans. We'll include the SLA summary in the docs we send.

[07:54] Mark Chen: Do you have examples of customers with similar workloads (market spikes + heavy embed)?
[07:59] Alex Morgan: Yes, we've worked with several fintechs — we'll anonymize two case studies showing cost delta and caching improvements.

[08:10] Elena Ruiz: For the pilot we'll need the Redwood SDK and a small runbook — instrumenting latency, token counts, and cache hit rate.
[08:17] Priya Desai: We'll provide a lightweight harness that plugs into your traffic replay and collects token-level metrics, latency histograms and per-request model selection.

[08:30] Sofia Park: On pricing, is there transparency into token pricing for different model families?
[08:35] Alex Morgan: Yes — our model catalog has per-token list prices and typical on-platform latency/cost profiles. In the tailored sheet we'll present effective per-1k chat costs under three cache and batching scenarios and compare Hosted vs Dedicated amortized costs.

[08:53] Mark Chen: Any hidden fees? Data egress? Storage?
[08:57] Alex Morgan: We'll call out egress (network) and storage for embeddings. Nothing unexpected — we'll itemize.

[09:08] Omar Al-Khalil: If we do Private on-prem, what's the timeline?
[09:13] Alex Morgan: On-prem is largest lift — usually 8-12 weeks for air-gapped or on-prem installs with security review. VPC/private control plane is faster, typically 2-4 weeks. We'll map options in the follow-up.

[09:30] Elena Ruiz: Are there any model fidelity regressions when using batching/quantization we should expect?
[09:36] Priya Desai: Very workload dependent. For embeddings, 8-bit quant often changes similarity scores slightly — we'll run A/B evals. For chat, quantized models may affect generation quality; we can propose guardrails and a quality threshold for fallback to full precision.

[09:55] Sofia Park: Ok let's recap next steps out loud.
[10:00] Alex Morgan: Recap: Redwood will send a tailored pricing spreadsheet with low/med/high cache scenarios, quantization and batching recommendations, SOC2/KMS/VPC docs, and a POC runbook. We'll schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-08-10. Priya will prepare the benchmark payloads. You (Ursa) will provide anonymized prompts and traffic profile. Action items captured in the crm.
[10:22] Mark Chen: Sounds good. Quick ask — can we get a sample of your latency histograms for the mid-tier models to compare to our 95/99 targets?
[10:30] Priya Desai: Yes, we'll attach typical latency histograms and a perf-run that emulates your open/close spike.

[10:40] Elena Ruiz: Great. Thanks everyone.
[10:43] Alex Morgan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the doc packet and sheet.

End of transcript.
